fixed.explanation: IndexCol.validate_metadata calls array_equivalent with dtype_equal=True even when the stored and new categories have different dtypes (int64 vs float64). That sends mismatched arrays into a Cython path and causes the buffer dtype error. I added a dtype check first, so mismatched dtypes count as different categories and raise the intended ValueError.

query.intent: HDFStore table-format append validates categorical column metadata against the stored categories (in pandas/io/pytables.py, e.g. validate_metadata / update_metadata on DataFrame columns). It compares the stored categories with new categories using a Cython hashtable/array_equivalent call that fails when dtypes differ (int64 vs float64). The comparison should handle dtype mismatch and raise the intended ValueError about differing categories.
query.symptom: Appending a categorical column with float categories to a table-format HDF5 store holding integer categories raises a "Buffer dtype mismatch, expected 'double' but got 'long'" ValueError instead of the "cannot append... categories differ" ValueError.

history.analysis: The results shown are only HDFStore.append/put wrappers and a test. The categories comparison lives in the table's metadata validation (validate_metadata / update_info / the 'metadata' handling in pytables.py), which likely calls array_equivalent on the old and new categories.
